context: Builds on static next hops, longest prefix matching and the point-to-point OSPF cost lab.
goal: Use the installed IPv4 table to restore the intended OSPF exit and keep a static fallback.

concepts.title: Read the source and network size
concepts.text: A routing table lists installed routes. C marks a directly connected network, L a local interface address, S a static route and O an intra-area OSPF route. S* marks the supplied static default. The /length and dotted-decimal mask describe the same size. For example, /26 leaves six zero bits in the mask, so the final mask octet is 192.

concepts.title: Read distance and metric separately
concepts.text: For the same exact network and mask, the router prefers the eligible source with the lower administrative distance. The first number in [110/23] is distance. The second is metric. OSPF adds outgoing costs along each path and the destination LAN cost, then offers its best path. Do not compare an OSPF cost directly with a static route's distance.

concepts.title: Look up a destination in the installed table
concepts.text: From the installed rows that contain an address, the longest prefix wins. A /26 can win inside its range while a /24 serves nearby addresses. A higher-distance static route for the same /26 can replace an OSPF row when the announcement is no longer available.

worked.label: Read the OSPF offer
worked.explanation: The shown path uses 5 + 9 + 7 = 21. The dotted mask is 255.255.255.192. The distance is 110.

worked.label: Keep a floating backup
worked.explanation: The static route has the same prefix and a higher distance. It becomes the installed /26 only after the OSPF announcement is withdrawn.

worked.label: Compare inside and outside
worked.explanation: A wider static /24 at distance 1 remains installed. Its smaller distance does not beat the longer prefix for .100.

practice.title: Stop the static route overriding the OSPF offer
practice.action: Look at Current installed decision. Enter 145 in Static backup distance.
practice.observe: The same-prefix OSPF offer replaces the static entry. The static backup stays ready.

practice.title: Change the preferred OSPF path
practice.action: Open Compare OSPF branch costs. The Maple path adds 7 and 5 after its outgoing cost. Enter 3 in Outgoing OSPF cost, then enter the /26 dotted mask in Inspect with network mask.
practice.observe: Maple now has the lower cost. The exact query displays the O row with metric 15.

practice.title: Compare the current and withdrawal tables
practice.action: Under Destination lookup, compare the first two addresses with the address ending in .128. Open Trial: withdraw the service announcement and try the inside addresses again. Select Check workspace.
practice.observe: Inside the service range, the current row uses OSPF and the trial uses the static backup. Outside it, the /24 stays in place.

requirements: Use the OSPF exit toward Harbor for both addresses inside the Records service network.
Keep the wider site route for the outside address. Keep the local, connected and default entries working.
Keep the supplied static backup usable when the service announcement is withdrawn.
Use the dotted-decimal mask to inspect the exact service entry.

review.introduction: Explains how to read route codes, mask, cost and distance using three worked observations.
review.example: Uses two actual OSPF paths, a static backup, destination lookups and a separate announcement-withdrawal trial.
review.assignment: Independent branch route control and exact mask query with inside, outside, local, connected and fallback checks.
